content: Embedded KV alternatives, verified: go.etcd.io/bbolt v1.5.0 takes an exclusive OS file lock so multiple processes cannot open the same DB concurrently, and ReadOnly mode uses a shared lock that blocks writers; dgraph-io/badger v4.9.6 is designed for single-process access. Neither supports the milestone requirement of concurrent multi-process read/write, so replacing SQLite WAL with them would fail the feature. A 2026 fork (aperturerobotics/bbolt) adds LMDB-style multi-process locking but is a 1-star project, not production material. Conclusion: SQLite WAL remains the right substrate; do not add a second storage engine.
